2610.12701.title: Activating the Annotator: Operationalising Lived Experience in Data Annotation
2610.12701.paper_summary: Perspectivist NLP has established that annotator positionality shapes labels for subjective tasks, but the field still lacks methods for operationalising it. Positionality is typically operationalised as a demographic form completed at recruitment: a static attribute recorded once and treated as a covariate, on the assumption that the knowledge it indexes is active when the annotator reads an item. This paper treats that assumption as a design problem and asks whether lived experience can instead be primed by the task itself. We introduce AXLE, a pre-annotation stage in which a scenario vignette anchors a short, axis-guided conversation that is synthesised into a first-person micro-narrative and returned to the annotator before labelling begins. In a 2x2 between-subjects study (104 annotators, 30 items, 1,040 annotations) on ambiguous hate speech spanning immigration, religion and gender, elicitation was associated with higher identity resonance and higher sensitivity to harm. It also increased label entropy and lowered inter-annotator agreement: the stage appears to surface plurality rather than manufacture consensus, which distinguishes it from annotator training, whose success criterion is convergence.
2610.12701.paper_summary_zh: 觀點主義自然語言處理已確立標註者的位置性會影響主觀任務的標籤，但該領域仍缺乏將其操作化的方法。位置性通常在招募時作為一種人口統計形式進行操作化：這是一個靜態屬性，僅記錄一次並視為協變量，假設它所指示的知識在標註者閱讀項目時是活躍的。本文將該假設視為設計問題，並詢問是否可以通過任務本身來引發生活經驗。我們介紹了AXLE，一個預標註階段，其中一個情境小品引導一段短暫的、以軸為導向的對話，並合成為第一人稱的微型敘事，在標註開始之前返回給標註者。在一項針對模糊仇恨言論的2x2被試間研究（104名標註者，30個項目，1,040個標註）中，涉及移民、宗教和性別，該引導與更高的身份共鳴和更高的對傷害的敏感性相關。它還增加了標籤的熵並降低了標註者之間的一致性：這一階段似乎揭示了多元性，而不是製造共識，這使其與標註者訓練區分開來，後者的成功標準是收斂。
